name: manual_fc919d
claim: PowerShell's [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(name, value, 'User') writes to the registry but does NOT refresh the CURRENT process's own $env: view -- an already-running shell keeps stale values, and any child process it spawns inherits the parent's stale in-memory env block, not a fresh registry read. Only a genuinely new top-level process (e.g. a fresh Task Scheduler tick) sees the update.

decisions.notes: Set corrected auth tokens via SetEnvironmentVariable(...,'User') mid-session, then re-ran coord_pulse.ps1 from the same long-lived shell and it still failed with the OLD token -- cost a full extra debug cycle before realizing the fix was to set $env:VAR directly in the same invoking block instead of trusting the registry write to propagate immediately.

rationale: Set corrected auth tokens via SetEnvironmentVariable(...,'User') mid-session, then re-ran coord_pulse.ps1 from the same long-lived shell and it still failed with the OLD token -- cost a full extra debug cycle before realizing the fix was to set $env:VAR directly in the same invoking block instead of trusting the registry write to propagate immediately.
